Title: Chapter 13 -multi-scale modeling of tissues using compucell3d
Abstract: The study of how cells interact to produce tissue development, homeostasis, or diseases was, until recently, almost purely experimental. Now, multi-cell computer simulation methods, ranging from relatively simple cellular automata to complex immersed-boundary and finite-element mechanistic models, allow in silico study of multi-cell phenomena at the tissue scale based on biologically observed cell behaviors and interactions such as movement, adhesion, growth, death, mitosis, secretion of chemicals, chemotaxis, etc. This tutorial introduces the lattice-based Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg (GGH) Monte Carlo multi-cell modeling and the open-source GGH-based CompuCell3D simulation environment that allows rapid and intuitive modeling and simulation of cellular and multi-cellular behaviors in the context of tissue formation and subsequent dynamics. We also present a walkthrough of four biological models and their associated simulations that demonstrate the capabilities of the GGH and CompuCell3D.

gold.abstract: Mechanistic, multicellular, agent-based models are commonly used to investigate tissue, organ, and organism-scale biology at single-cell resolution. The Cellular-Potts Model (CPM) is a powerful and popular framework for developing and interrogating these models. CPMs become computationally expensive at large space- and time- scales making application and investigation of developed models difficult. Surrogate models may allow for the accelerated evaluation of CPMs of complex biological systems. However, the stochastic nature of these models means each set of parameters may give rise to different model configurations, complicating surrogate model development. In this work, we leverage denoising diffusion probabilistic models to train a generative AI surrogate of a CPM used to investigate in vitro vasculogenesis. We describe the use of an image classifier to learn the characteristics that define unique areas of a 2-dimensional parameter space. We then apply this classifier to aid in surrogate model selection and verification. Our CPM model surrogate generates model configurations 20,000 timesteps ahead of a reference configuration and demonstrates approximately a 22x reduction in computational time as compared to native code execution. Our work represents a step towards the implementation of DDPMs to develop digital twins of stochastic biological systems.

We then apply this classifier to aid in surrogate model selection and verification.
gold.title: Generative diffusion model surrogates for mechanistic agent-based biological models

--- Researcher B ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b (CompuCell3D): Provides a lattice-based Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg (GGH) Monte Carlo framework for multi-scale tissue modeling. It simulates cell behaviors (adhesion, growth, mitosis, secretion, chemotaxis) and tissue dynamics using biologically observed parameters, enabling in silico experiments on multicellular systems.
- Paper-c (Deep learning transport): Introduces conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN) to directly infer and generate solutions to steady-state heat conduction and incompressible fluid flow from observational data, bypassing governing equations. The model learns mappings from boundary conditions and domain geometry to field solutions.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
We propose using cGAN as a learned surrogate for the chemical diffusion and reaction fields that drive cell behavior in GGH simulations. In CompuCell3D, cell secretion and chemotaxis depend on solving partial differential equations (PDEs) for diffusible morphogens. The cGAN, trained on high-fidelity PDE solutions or experimental concentration data, would replace the numerical PDE solver inside GGH. This creates a hybrid simulation where cell dynamics (GGH) are coupled to a deep-learned transport field generator (cGAN), enabling faster and possibly data-driven tissue patterning without explicit PDE solving.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Training data: Generate synthetic morphogen concentration fields by solving steady-state diffusion-decay PDEs on 2D lattices with varied cell-secretion sources and boundary conditions. Alternatively, use image-based experimental gradients.
- Model: Train a cGAN (as in paper-c) to map source distributions and domain masks to concentration fields.
- Coupling: In CompuCell3D, each Monte Carlo step calls the trained cGAN to update the morphogen field based on current cell secretion states; cells then respond via chemotaxis or differentiation rules.
- Validation: Compare tissue patterns (e.g., cell sorting, vascular-like network formation) from hybrid model vs. full PDE-based GGH simulation. Metrics: pattern similarity, cell fate distribution, and computational speedup.
- Missing cross-paper knowledge: We do not have details on cGAN architecture or training specifics from paper-c beyond abstract; nor do we know CompuCell3D’s API for external field solvers. These would need to be obtained from full texts or developer documentation.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project couples a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) trained on morphogen transport data with the Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg (GGH) cellular Potts model in CompuCell3D. The cGAN acts as a learned surrogate for diffusion-reaction fields, replacing numerical PDE solvers during tissue simulation. We hypothesize that this hybrid approach maintains biologically accurate multicellular patterning while significantly reducing computational cost and enabling data-driven field inference. Validation will compare cell sorting and network formation against classical GGH-PDE simulations.

FINAL IDEA: Integrate a cGAN-based learned transport solver into the GGH cellular Potts framework to replace PDE-based morphogen diffusion, enabling faster and data-driven multi-scale tissue simulations.

--- Researcher C ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- paper-b: CompuCell3D provides a lattice-based Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg (GGH) Monte Carlo framework for multi-scale tissue modeling. It simulates cell behaviors (adhesion, growth, mitosis, chemotaxis, secretion) and tissue dynamics, validated against biological observations.
- paper-c: Conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN) infer and directly generate solutions to steady-state heat conduction and incompressible fluid flow from observations alone, without governing equations, achieving high accuracy for arbitrary boundary conditions and domains.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
We propose using cGAN as a learned surrogate for the chemical/diffusive microenvironment within CompuCell3D tissue simulations. In GGH models, cell behavior depends on local chemical fields (e.g., morphogens, nutrients) that are typically solved by finite-difference diffusion equations. Instead, a cGAN trained on high-fidelity transport solutions (from paper-c’s paradigm) could rapidly generate chemical field distributions given arbitrary tissue geometry, boundary conditions, and source/sink patterns produced by cells. This couples paper-c’s data-driven transport solver to paper-b’s cell-based tissue dynamics: cells secrete/consume chemicals, altering local conditions, which the cGAN then predicts, feeding back to cell decisions (proliferation, differentiation, migration).

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Build a hybrid CompuCell3D model of a growing epithelial sheet with a diffusing growth factor.
- Train a cGAN on paired (domain geometry, boundary conditions, source distribution) → steady-state concentration fields, using synthetic data from finite-difference solutions (paper-c’s method).
- In simulation, at each Monte Carlo step, extract cell positions and secretion rates to define sources; pass geometry and sources to the trained cGAN to predict chemical field; use field to update cell behaviors (e.g., mitosis probability).
- Validate by comparing hybrid model outputs (tissue growth rate, patterning) against a fully PDE-based CompuCell3D control for identical initial conditions.
- Metrics: chemical field MAE, tissue morphology similarity, computational speedup.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose integrating a conditional GAN-based transport solver (paper-c) into the CompuCell3D multi-scale tissue modeling environment (paper-b). The cGAN learns to predict steady-state chemical fields directly from tissue geometry and cell secretion patterns, bypassing iterative PDE solvers. This hybrid framework is tested on an epithelial growth model, comparing accuracy and speed against traditional finite-difference coupling. The contribution is a novel, data-driven microenvironment engine for cell-based tissue simulations that may accelerate large-scale, multi-parameter studies.

Missing cross-paper knowledge: paper-c’s cGAN was demonstrated for heat conduction and fluid flow, not for reaction-diffusion with moving cellular sources; transferability to dynamic, discrete source distributions must be established. Also, paper-b’s GGH uses stochastic updates, requiring many chemical field evaluations per step; cGAN inference speed and error propagation in this loop are untested.

FINAL IDEA: Couple a cGAN-trained transport solver into CompuCell3D to replace PDE-based chemical field computation, enabling faster, data-driven feedback between tissue geometry, cell secretion, and multicellular behavior.

SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- paper-b: CompuCell3D (CC3D) implements GGH Monte Carlo cell dynamics with cell behaviors (adhesion, mitosis, chemotaxis, secretion) and built-in PDE solvers for diffusible fields.
- paper-c: Conditional GANs (cGAN) learn direct mappings from boundary/domain conditions to steady-state transport solutions (heat, fluid flow) without iterative PDE solving, achieving low MAE.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
I adopt Researcher A’s cGAN-as-surrogate concept but reject their “initial-to-final tissue state” mapping because it eliminates the feedback between chemical fields and cell decisions that defines GGH. I qualify my prior proposal (cGAN replaces PDE every step) by introducing a quasi-steady approximation: the cGAN predicts the chemical field from the current cell-secreted source map only when sources change above a threshold (e.g., after cell division, death, or significant migration). Between updates, the field is held fixed. This reduces inference frequency and error accumulation while preserving the data-driven transport paradigm from paper-c. The causal coupling is: GGH cell states → source map → cGAN → chemical field → GGH cell updates.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
- Generate training data using CC3D’s built-in steady-state diffusion solver: for a cell sorting model with two cell types secreting activator/inhibitor, record (source map, domain mask) → concentration field pairs from many random cell configurations.
- Train paper-c’s cGAN architecture on these pairs; validate on held-out snapshots with MAE and SSIM.
- Integrate into CC3D via a Python steppable: every N=20 Monte Carlo steps, compute source map from current cell positions, call cGAN, update field; cells respond via chemotaxis and adhesion.
- Compare hybrid vs. full PDE simulation: (i) chemical field MAE at sampled steps, (ii) final cell sorting index (interface length, cluster size), (iii) wall-clock speedup.
- Test robustness: vary secretion rates, cell densities, and N (update frequency) to find accuracy–speed trade-off.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
We propose a hybrid tissue simulator that embeds a conditional GAN, trained on CompuCell3D’s diffusion solver outputs, as a quasi-steady surrogate for morphogen fields within GGH dynamics. Unlike full-dynamics surrogates, our cGAN only replaces the PDE step and is invoked when cellular sources change significantly, preserving cell-level stochasticity and feedback. We validate on a two-cell-type activator–inhibitor sorting assay, measuring field accuracy, emergent pattern fidelity, and speedup. This integration demonstrates that data-driven transport solvers can accelerate multi-scale tissue models without sacrificing biological feedback, extending paper-c’s static-domain results to dynamic, discrete sources.

Missing knowledge: paper-c’s cGAN was not tested with discrete, moving sources or repeated inference in a stochastic loop; we explicitly test generalization and error accumulation under these conditions.

FINAL IDEA: Embed a cGAN trained on CompuCell3D steady-state diffusion solutions as a quasi-steady chemical field surrogate, invoked only when cell-secreted sources change, to accelerate GGH tissue simulations while preserving cell–field feedback.
